_comment: One entry per autonomy x impact intersection. "posture" and "risk" are the reconciled values from the final report (Appendix C Table C1 and Appendix E Table E1) and apply to all 24 cells. "annotated" says whether a scenario card was written for the cell: false means the scenario, controls, approval and rollback below are the generic tier floor, not cell-specific research. Every key in "sources" must exist in literature.json or the build fails. Set "status" to "draft" on anything not yet reviewed - lib/content.js redacts draft cells out of a published build.

cells.scenario: Internal read-only research or FAQ assistant.
controls: AI disclosure at first contact
Retrieval-scoped; abstain if no source
Out-of-scope refusal in code, not prompt
Named owner
Prompt / response logging
Version-pinned rollback
cells.approval: None per response. Approval attaches to content, not output.
cells.rollback: Revert to last known-good knowledge base and model version.

cells.scenario: Internal policy, HR or IT helpdesk assistant.
controls: Mandatory source citation
Abstain and escalate, never guess
Named escalation route
SME content sign-off + freshness SLA
Sampled QA review
Targeted user correction
cells.approval: Subject-matter expert signs off content changes, recorded with date and version.
cells.rollback: Revert, then correct identifiable affected users through the existing support channel.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored: supervised. Review copy and tool sheet: permitted. Resolved to supervised — evidenced by Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024): an organisation owns what its information-only chatbot says.

cells.scenario: Public-facing information service at scale.
controls: High-stakes topics fenced to a human channel
Red-team eval per release
Live groundedness monitoring
Staged / canary rollout
Two-person release gate
Tested kill switch
Cohort-level correction
cells.approval: Two-person gate on anything changing the public answer surface.
cells.rollback: Versioned revert, kill switch to static content, cohort-level correction reconstructed from logs.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored: restricted. Review copy and tool sheet: supervised. Resolved to restricted — evidenced by the NYC MyCity incident (Lecher, 2024): an information-only public-sector bot giving unlawful guidance at scale, with disclaimers, left online after publication.

cells.scenario: Safeguarding, crisis or health information; vulnerable users.
controls: Impact assessment before launch
Professional-authored safety content
Deterministic crisis routing
Long-session / adversarial testing
Accountable owner, 24/7 suspension
Independent evaluation
Pre-tested fallback to human channel
cells.approval: Named professional owner with 24/7 suspension authority; two-person sign-off on safety-path changes.
cells.rollback: Pre-tested fallback to static resources and a staffed human channel. Rollback protects the next user, not the one already harmed.

cells.scenario: Advisory risk score or case-law memo generated by the system; stored but not yet reviewed or accessed by any court officer.
controls: AI disclosure: output labeled AI-generated advisory
Retrieval scoped to approved legal databases; public GenAI tools excluded
Framed as advisory and non-determinative in every instance
Named system owner recorded in AI system register
Prompt / response logging with retrieved source IDs
Version-pinned risk model and knowledge base with tested revert path
cells.approval: No per-response approval; sign-off attaches to risk-model, knowledge-base, and prompt version, recorded with date and authority.
cells.rollback: Version-pinned risk model, KB, and prompt with a tested revert path; named owner holds 24/7 suspension authority.

cells.scenario: Judicial clerk accesses the risk score or case-law memo to prepare an internal research brief; output hasn't reached the presiding judge.
controls: Mandatory source citation for every retrieved case or statute
Citation-verification: every case cross-referenced against a validated legal database before the memo is finalised
Abstain and flag if no approved source; never generate unsourced legal claims
Named escalation route from clerk to senior clerk or judge
SME (qualified legal officer) content verification before the memo leaves the research stage
Sampled QA review of output accuracy and abstention rate
cells.approval: Every advisory logged — court ID, case reference, query, output, scored factors, source IDs, model version, timestamp. Role-based access on logs.
cells.rollback: Same as I0 — version-pinned revert path and 24/7 kill-switch authority.

cells.scenario: Presiding judge accesses the advisory risk score during a live bail or sentencing hearing; a defendant's liberty is under active consideration.
controls: All I0/I1 controls, plus mandatory written disclosure that the score is proprietary and non-determinative
Score methodology limits explained alongside every output
Independent validation / re-norming of the risk model for the jurisdiction, disclosed to the court if absent
Defendant's right to review and contest scored factors; defence's right to cross-examine methodology
Periodic audit of score-to-outcome correlation to detect anchoring patterns
Red-team evaluation: protected-characteristic proxies, unusual criminal histories, and other edge cases
cells.approval: As I1, plus the judge's independent written justification for the decision logged separately; exception log for any advisory used as the sole/determinative factor (a Loomis violation).
cells.rollback: Same tested revert path and kill switch as I1.

cells.scenario: Judge has relied on the advisory risk score for a bail or sentencing decision that has been served or executed; outcome is irreversible.
controls: Score cannot be the sole or determinative factor; judge must independently justify the decision in writing
Dual-review for high-stakes decisions (custody, long sentences)
Post-decision audit trail linking score inputs, advisory output, and judicial outcome
Disputed racial-disparity finding disclosed as an unresolved empirical question, not settled fact
Tested kill switch: named owner with 24/7 authority to suspend the scoring system
Mandatory incident reporting for any case where score and outcome are later found wrongly aligned
Regulatory anchor: classified high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III 8(a); meets the Art. 6(3) 'materially influence' test
cells.approval: Same as I2.
cells.rollback: As prior levels, plus: reconstruct affected cases from logs, notify affected courts, flag for judicial review; mandatory incident reporting. Fallback — court reverts to pre-AI procedure with no dependency on the tool.

cells.scenario: Agent drafts a routine equipment-calibration log entry or formats a training-record summary from raw MES data, for a supervisor to glance over and file. No batch, deviation, or regulatory document involved — purely internal housekeeping paperwork.
controls: Spot-check review, not full verification
No write access to batch records or QMS
Logging of draft vs. final diff
Named owner
cells.approval: Low-stakes drafts get a quick supervisor check, not a formal sign-off.
cells.rollback: Draft/final diff is logged, so any bad draft is traceable and correctable before filing.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored: permitted with light-touch verification. Review copy: supervised. Tool matrix sheet: permitted. Resolved to supervised — unevidenced, judgement.

cells.scenario: Agent drafts a minor environmental-monitoring trend annotation or a routine SOP-revision redline (formatting/clarity only, no procedural change) for a QA reviewer to approve before it enters the document management system.
controls: Mandatory human read-through before filing (not a rubber stamp)
Every factual claim traceable to a specific EM log or SOP section
No e-signature credential
Sampled QA audit of finalized entries
cells.approval: Recorded chain — who reviewed it, against what source data, and when.
cells.rollback: Same as I0, plus the recorded review chain lets a bad entry be traced and pulled before it is finalized.

cells.scenario: Agent drafts a change-control impact summary for a non-critical equipment or utility change (e.g. a calibration schedule adjustment), grounded in MES/LIMS data, for a process engineer to verify and formally submit into the QMS change-control module.
controls: Independent verification against source batch/process data, not just a read-through
No write access to validated setpoints or the master batch record
Immutable audit trail: draft → reviewer edits → submission
Hard escalation if source data conflicts across MES/LIMS
cells.approval: Recorded chain of who reviewed, against what source data, and when — same mechanism as I1, applied more strictly given higher stakes.
cells.rollback: Version-pinned draft; conflicting source data forces hard escalation before submission, preventing bad drafts from reaching change-control. Named owner can suspend the drafting feature if error patterns emerge.

cells.scenario: Agent drafts a deviation investigation report, CAPA proposal, or batch-record discrepancy note grounded in the batch record, SOPs, and regulatory requirements; the Qualified Person must verify every citation against source and apply the e-signature before batch disposition. The draft is reversible; the release decision it feeds is not.
controls: No e-signature or release credential — technical, not policy, separation
Hard escalation when the deviation is major/critical, grounding is weak, or the event touches sterility/patient safety
Immutable FDA Part-11 audit trail linking draft → reviewer verification → signed final (proves verification happened, not a rubber stamp)
Documented model-credibility case per FDA's 2025 AI guidance; periodic QA audit of drafted vs. finalized documents to catch review drift
cells.approval: Qualified Person applies e-signature only after verifying every citation against source; the agent itself never holds signing authority.
cells.rollback: Audit trail lets any wrongly-signed document be traced from draft through reviewer edits to the final signature, and flagged for correction. If the system is suspended, staff revert to writing these documents manually, with no dependency on the tool.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored: draft-only with mandatory verified sign-off. Review copy: prohibited / redesign. Resolved to mandatory verified sign-off — the permitting cell cites 21 C.F.R. pt. 11, Mata v. Avianca and draft FDA guidance on model credibility; the prohibiting cell recorded no scenario, controls or citation.

cells.scenario: No scenario card is published for this intersection. The posture and the controls below are the tier-2 floor the matrix sets.
controls: Supervision proportionate to the action, with a reviewer who can challenge and stop it
Declared limits on what the agent may touch
Validation of outputs before they are relied on
Audit logs with exception monitoring
Documented and tested rollback
cells.approval: Supervised or conditional deployment: an accountable reviewer with the authority and visibility to intervene.
cells.rollback: Documented and tested revert path, exercised before go-live.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored: auto-approved / supervised. Review copy: supervised. Tool matrix sheet: permitted. Resolved to supervised — unevidenced, judgement.

cells.scenario: No scenario card is published for this intersection. The posture and the controls below are the tier-3 floor the matrix sets.
controls: Formal assurance or verified sign-off before deployment
Least privilege with an action allowlist
Defined action thresholds with anomaly and duplicate checks
Real-time monitoring and alerting
Tested rollback and a kill switch
Independent validation separate from the build team
cells.approval: Restricted deployment: recorded approval at the stated authority level, with evidence reviewed and timestamped.
cells.rollback: Tested rollback plus emergency isolation, both exercised before go-live.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored and review copy: restricted. Tool matrix sheet: supervised. Resolved to restricted — unevidenced, judgement.

cells.scenario: Alert enrichment: the agent gathers and attaches context to screening alerts.
controls: Formal assurance and sign-off before deployment
Continuous monitoring
Immutable audit log
Kill switch
cells.approval: None per enrichment action. Approval attaches to the retrieval and enrichment scope, not each output.
cells.rollback: Revert to last known-good screening configuration; kill switch to suspend enrichment pending review.
cells.reconciliation: Column-authored and review copy: restricted. Tool matrix sheet: supervised / conditional. Resolved to restricted — unevidenced, judgement.

cells.scenario: Narrow-rule closure: the agent closes alerts that match an approved rule.
controls: Human approval on the closure rule itself, though instances execute autonomously
Transaction and volume limits
Immutable approval logs, tagged machine-closed
Tested rollback
cells.approval: None per closure instance. Approval attaches to the closure policy: who signed off the confidence threshold and scope, when, at what authority.
cells.rollback: Version-pinned closure rule with a tested revert path; reopen any closed alert from the immutable log.

cells.scenario: Transaction hold: the agent places a hold on a customer transaction.
controls: Reduce autonomy to L3 or lower — a hold requires human approval before execution
Mandatory sign-off before any hold is placed
Transaction and value limits defining what may be flagged versus escalated
Immutable approval log: who approved, evidence reviewed, timestamp
Stop conditions — a hold auto-expires or escalates if not actioned
Kill switch
Tested rollback: fast hold release with customer notification
cells.approval: Mandatory human sign-off per hold, with approver, authority level, timestamp and evidence reviewed.
cells.rollback: Reverse a wrongly-placed hold immediately; reconstruct affected accounts from logs if a batch is found flawed.

cells.scenario: Full-policy closure: autonomous SAR filing or account restriction.
controls: No autonomous execution at this scope — reduce to L3 or lower
Dual human approval for SAR filing or account restriction
Fail closed: incomplete evidence defaults to escalation, never autonomous closure
Independent, continuous second-line model-risk validation, separate from the build team
Full reasoning-trace logging, not just the final decision
Mandatory incident reporting and board-level escalation on systemic error
cells.approval: Dual human sign-off before filing or restriction executes. Named approvers, authority levels, timestamps and evidence reviewed, logged separately from routine closure logs.
cells.rollback: Reconstruct affected accounts and transactions from logs; flag for manual review; mandatory incident reporting. Fallback is fully human-reviewed closure with no operational dependency on the agent.

cells.scenario: No scenario card is published for this intersection. The posture and the controls below are the tier-4 floor the matrix sets.
controls: Do not deploy in the assessed configuration
Reduce autonomy, or reduce the impact class, before reassessment
Where the action must exist, move it behind explicit human approval
Fail closed: incomplete evidence escalates rather than executes
cells.approval: Not applicable: no control strength returns a deployable posture at this intersection.
cells.rollback: Not a substitute for redesign. The operating envelope must change before reassessment.
